name: Caro-Kann Classical
summary: The Caro-Kann Classical (1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5): rock-solid defence with the good bishop out early.
intro: The Caro-Kann Classical Variation arises after 1.e4 c6 2.d4 d5 3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4 Bf5, the venerable heart of the Caro-Kann. Rather than shut in the light-squared bishop as in the French, Black liberates it to f5 before playing ...e6, resolving the defence's chief structural problem at the outset. The result is one of the soundest replies to 1.e4: Black cedes a touch of space in exchange for a resilient structure and a genuinely active piece.
line: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5

sections.heading: Strategic ideas
paragraphs: The defining decision is 4...Bf5, developing the queen's bishop outside the pawn chain before ...e6 boxes it in. This gives the Classical its enduring reputation for solidity: Black obtains a compact, weakness-free structure and, crucially, an active good bishop that so often languishes in 1.e4 e6 defences. From there Black follows a well-worn set-up with ...e6, ...Nd7, ...Ngf6, ...Bd6 and ...Qc7, frequently castling queenside to bring the rooks to bear along the central and half-open files.

White's counterplay flows naturally from the position. By harassing the f5-bishop with Ng3 and the pawn advance h4-h5, White gains kingside space and questions Black's most valued piece, often coaxing it to g6 where it can be traded or restricted. The middlegame becomes a contest between White's spatial edge and kingside expansion and Black's sturdy, elastic structure; if Black can neutralise the pressure on the bishop and complete development, the ending typically favours the side with fewer weaknesses.

sections.heading: Main variations
paragraphs: The principal tabiya is reached after 5.Ng3 Bg6 6.h4 h6 7.Nf3 Nd7, when White has staked out kingside space and Black continues the standard development with ...e6, ...Ngf6, ...Bd6 and ...Qc7. This is the classical Capablanca treatment, prized for its reliability, and it long served as the mainstream answer to the whole variation.

White has several distinct tries against the set-up. The sharp 7.h5 Bh7 8.Nf3 lines, followed by Bd3 to exchange the h7-bishop, remain a critical test of Black's resources, while quieter development with Bd3 and c3 keeps a small, stable edge. Black, for his part, must handle the standard structures accurately, and modern practice has also explored ...Bd6 and ...Qc7 arrangements that prepare timely ...c5 or ...e5 breaks to free the position.

sections.heading: History and background
paragraphs: The Classical Variation is the oldest and most respected way of handling the Caro-Kann, and its association with Jose Raul Capablanca gives it the alternate name Capablanca Variation. For generations it has embodied the defence's core philosophy of trading a little space for a sound, low-risk position and an unusually well-placed light-squared bishop, and it endures at every level as one of the most trusted answers to 1.e4.
